official.deadline_note: Applications are possible only between 1 June and the stated annual application deadline; DAAD updates deadlines annually in the second quarter on the programme page. The portal is currently closed between cycles.
official.application_cycle: Annual cycle; funding must begin in 2027, usually on 1 October 2027, for winter term 2027/28 only
official.status_note: The DAAD page states that you currently cannot apply for this programme and refers to the application deadline shown under the Application procedure tab; the portal only appears during the annual window.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The DAAD does not cover tuition fees; only tuition-free Master's degree programmes qualify.
benefits: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance cover

On application: monthly rent subsidy, monthly allowance for accompanying family members, subsidy for justified costs in case of disability or chronic illness, reimbursement of carbon offset payments for air travel

Language benefits on application: payment of online language course fees, a German language course in Germany before the programme, an allowance for a personally chosen German course, and reimbursement of TestDaF or DSH test fees
eligibility: High-achieving students from developing and emerging countries; country eligibility is checked against the DAAD list (e.g. Ghana, Kenya, Indonesia, Mexico, Vietnam, Peru, Colombia, Jordan and others)
First degree recognised in Germany (e.g. Bachelor's degree) completed by the application deadline at the latest
Cannot already hold a Master's degree by the application deadline
Most recent university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline
Cannot have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline

Admission to a full-time, on-campus Master's in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering at a German state or state-recognised university, starting winter term 2027/28; the programme must be tuition-free and must not have already begun in Germany
requirements: Only complete applications with all mandatory documents are considered; incomplete applications are excluded for formal reasons
Proof of at least level B1 in the language of instruction must be provided to the DAAD when applying for the scholarship
Applicants are themselves responsible for submitting the university admission application by its due date
documents: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages)
Letter of admission to the study programme at the host university (or submitted before the funding period begins)
Form 'Information about your preferred master programmes' (up to 5 programmes)
Current transcript of records with individual grades
All university degree certificates already obtained, with transcripts for all academic years (provisional document if not yet issued)
Language certificate for the language of instruction (no older than 3 years, at least B1)
One recent letter of recommendation on the DAAD form from a university teacher
Passport or national identity card (for refugees: refugee ID card and UNHCR registration or official proof of asylum)
selection_criteria: Academic qualification: academic achievements, course of studies, knowledge of the language of instruction, relevant internships and work experience
Quality of the study project and of the preparation: choice of degree programme, host university and establishment of contacts, and integration into the academic career path
Potential of the applicant: motivation, prospects for further development, extracurricular commitment

Equal-opportunity aspects are considered; the committee can take account of special life circumstances such as disability, chronic illness, raising children, refugee background or work undertaken to finance studies
coverage: Payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
Tuition fees are not covered - the DAAD does not cover tuition and formally excludes Master's programmes that charge fees
application_method: Register in the DAAD portal between 1 June and the application deadline
Generate the letter of recommendation form in the portal and send it to your university teacher
Complete the online application and upload all documents as PDF files
Submit online - the portal closes at 24:00 CET/CEST on the last application day
official.application_route: Online through the DAAD portal during the annual window; applications are only possible from the listed eligible countries
official.citizenship_residency: Eligibility depends on the country you live in and apply from, which must appear on the DAAD list for this programme
official.international_eligibility: Yes - aimed at international students from developing and emerging countries
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: STEM disciplines only: mathematics, computer science, natural sciences and engineering; interdisciplinary programmes require a designated STEM focus; funded by the German Federal Foreign Office
official.duration: Funding is provided for 10 months to a maximum of 24 months depending on the standard period of study, usually beginning 1 October 2027 or earlier with a prior German language course
official.description: The programme supports the qualification and employability of young academics from developing and emerging countries by funding a complete, tuition-free STEM Master's degree at a German university.
official.program_type: Government-funded Master's scholarship (German Federal Foreign Office, administered by DAAD)
official.english_requirement: At least level B1 in the language of instruction must be proven to the DAAD when applying; the language of instruction is German, or English in international programmes, and accepted English certificates include IELTS, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge and Duolingo English Test

verification.notes: The DAAD scholarship database entry (detail 57742130) was fetched live; monthly amount, allowances, eligibility, documents and selection process were confirmed on DAAD's own domain. The exact annual application date is not published inline - DAAD states it updates deadlines in the second quarter - so the date is recorded as not confirmed.

applicant_utility.summary: Two gates decide this scholarship before you write a single line: your country of application must be on DAAD's eligible list, and every programme you name must be tuition-free at a state or state-recognised university, because DAAD formally excludes programmes that charge fees. The monthly award is EUR 992 plus insurance payments, a travel allowance on application and an annual study allowance of EUR 460 - enough to live on in Germany but not to also cover fees. Since the portal only opens on 1 June and closes hard at midnight on the deadline day, treat late May as your real target for a complete dossier, and expect an interview with an independent committee of university teachers after document pre-selection.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent STEM graduates (typically within six years of the first degree) from a listed developing or emerging country who want a tuition-free German Master's.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country of application appears in the eligible-country list on the DAAD page before investing effort
Shortlist only full-time, on-campus, tuition-free STEM Master's programmes starting in winter term 2027/28 and note their separate university admission deadlines
Request the DAAD recommendation form from your professor through the portal once the window opens - it can only be generated then
Secure at least a B1 language certificate for the language of instruction, no older than three years
Prepare every listed document as PDF; incomplete applications are formally excluded
common_rejection_risks: Naming any programme that charges tuition fees - formally excluded from consideration
An incomplete dossier, since all listed documents are mandatory
Already holding a Master's degree, or a first degree older than roughly six years
More than 15 months of residence in Germany at the deadline
No admission letter by the time funding begins
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition wherever a programme charges it, visa and language test fees that DAAD does not reimburse, and the period before the first monthly payment
document_audit: If your degree certificate is not yet issued, upload a provisional document and supply the original before the scholarship starts
The recommendation letter must be on the official DAAD form generated inside the portal
Transcripts must show individual grades per academic year, not only final averages
Documents in your national language need German or English translations uploaded together with the originals
alerts: The portal is only available from 1 June until the annual deadline - outside that window there is no way to apply
Funding begins in 2027, usually 1 October 2027, and only for winter term 2027/28 starts
The personal interview is described as a decisive element of assessment, not a formality
Academic achievements after the first year are reassessed before the scholarship continues
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the DAAD portal from 1 June, generate the recommendation form, upload all documents and submit before the deadline; document pre-selection follows, then an interview with the independent selection committee.
